sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 767-780. Pacific Linguistics C-38.

Phylum-level phonological summary on p. 769 covers only segments (three places of articulation, usually no voicing contrast, five to eight vowels, many fricatives), illustrated from Olo; Muniwara appears only in the classification list, p. 774 (Marienberg stock-level family, 826 speakers).
